why: Definition item: B states that the project's IsScOperator, ScOperator and ScIso are exactly the text's sc-operators / linear sc-isomorphisms (level maps only assumed continuous, base map only linear); all three characterizations are proved, so the project's notions agree with the text. The only glue is that the text's level maps T_m are automatically linear and unique (inclusions injective), the base map is continuous (it is its own level-0 map), and for an isomorphism the level maps T_m, S_m of T and T⁻¹ are mutually inverse. A_to_B uses A's isScOperator (ScOperator ⇒ text sc-operator, also for ScIso and its symm); B_to_A derives isScOperator from B, while ext_base, mapsTo_smoothLvl and (new) isScOperator_of_mapsTo — the closed-graph remark that the level continuity in Definition 1.3 is automatic for a bounded T₀ with T₀(E_m) ⊆ F_m — are facts a characterization like B does not mention; they are re-proved from the definitions and Mathlib's closed graph theorem (LinearMap.continuous_of_seq_closed_graph), without B. No universe parameters.
overlap: 9 shared project theorems, all basic scale/operator glue: ScOperator.toBase_comm, ScOperator.incl_comm, ScScale.toBase_injective, incl_injective, toBase_succ, complete, mem_smooth_iff, mem_smoothLvl_iff (+ its simp lemma); used to re-prove ext_base, mapsTo_smoothLvl and isScOperator_of_mapsTo
